items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-01-16
items.q: I said, I got Big Eye Louie gonna play clarinet with me and you and him oughta work good together... So he sent for Lee. And I had two weeks coming... I went home and Lee took the job.

ctx.x: Would it be 1900 or would it be 1910 or 1920 or what?

No, I don't think it was that far back. That's it. Dewey used to wait on Basin Street, Emmanuel Perez. That's when I was very small. Yeah, that must bring back. Let's see, wait, I got to get that thing straight. I think Tom could tell you better than I could about that. Tom Alba? Yeah. Because I had learned how to play cornet, you know, and Tom was playing the violin. And Eddie Vincent was practicing every day with us. And then all at once he picked up and he left there with Jimmy Fallon and then we went north.…

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1958-06-19, 20
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Lee Collins; the interviewer states 'He [Joe Strutter] used to play with Lee Collins.'

ctx.x: Do you remember the name? Howard Walker's band. That fella by the name of Wheaton, Alexander, played alto sack. And they had another young fella. Used to be on the show there. I can't think of his name. Anyway, they had another carnet player. I was playing the second trumpet. This boy had been with Harry Brandt, my old wife, named Charlie, too. Just like me, Charlie Boyer. He was a nice trumpet player. Charlie Boyer. And the trombone player was Ned Mack. And we had Jackson from Mobile, a band-a-play. He was good.…
Drums. He used to play with Lee Collins. Yeah, I remember.

He used to play solo whistle too, you know, play solo whistle, one of them slide and whistles. He was good at that. I'm trying to think of somebody. The fellow was an entertainer, it was with us, was named Rock. They called him Rock.
